clue.text: Aussie friend has clothes, etc, left out

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for left is dropped from the clothing word

parts.note: clobber is British slang for clothes and personal gear

explanation.surface: An Australian mate turns up having left some of his clothes and belongings behind.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOBBER is informal British for clothes and kit; 'out' removes its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobber is Australian slang for a mate or companion.

clue.text: Do better than one notorious gangster

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or top it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to outdo a single infamous mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the Prohibition-era Chicago mob boss, the most famous gangster of all.

clue.text: Competition in which there should be a fair winner

definitions.text: Competition in which there should be a fair winner

parts.words: Competition in which there should be a fair winner
parts.note: fair seems to mean just or unbiased, but here it means beautiful, so the winner is the loveliest entrant

explanation.surface: Any contest ought to be won fairly, without cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' reads as honest; its old sense of lovely is the one meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant judging looks crowns the most attractive entrant, a fair one in the poetic sense.

clue.text: Group's manager's records, note, at home

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
te is a spelling of the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
in means at home

explanation.surface: A band's manager keeps their records and a note of things at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The group is the Beatles, managed by Brian Epstein.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Epstein managed the Beatles, the most famous pop group of the sixties.

clue.text: Performer in Rwandan ceremony

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning Rwandan and ceremony

explanation.surface: An artist takes part in an African ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer is one kind of stage performer.

clue.text: Stare in wonder after a religious feast

indicators.note: after places the staring word behind the single letter in the clue

parts.note: to gape is to stare open-mouthed in amazement

explanation.surface: Someone gawps in amazement following a holy banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stare in wonder' looks like the definition, as the answer can mean open-mouthed; it is wordplay here.
explanation.definitionFit: The agape was the love feast shared by early Christians.

clue.text: Northern city puts up, for election, furniture to sit in

parts.note: Chester is a city in Cheshire, north-west England
a party fields candidates when it puts them up for election

explanation.surface: A northern English city puts forward candidates in an election.
explanation.walkthrough: CHESTER is a cathedral city in Cheshire, in England's north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: A chesterfield is a deep buttoned leather sofa with arms level with its back.

clue.text: Live as president putting some characters off

indicators.note: putting off some characters means dropping a few letters, here from both ends of the word president

explanation.surface: A head of state puts certain people off living in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting some characters off' strips P from the front and NT from the end of PRESIDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to dwell or have your home there.

clue.text: Quietly brought up and given approval

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
raised means reared or brought up

explanation.surface: A child raised quietly and with approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To be praised is to receive commendation.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical female's cases done differently

indicators.note: doing the letters differently means arranging them in another order

explanation.surface: A churchwoman handles her caseload in her own way.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaconess is a woman holding a ministerial office in some churches.

clue.text: Regions in South Africa with time turned around

indicators.note: turned around says the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Parts of South Africa where the clocks went back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned around' turns SAERA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Areas and regions are both districts or zones.

clue.text: Chemical surprisingly inert

indicators.note: surprisingly hints the letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A substance that unexpectedly does not react.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is saltpetre, potassium nitrate, a compound used in gunpowder.

clue.text: Declare 1950s-style youth should be turned away

parts.note: to aver is to state or assert
a Ted, Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress

explanation.surface: Someone states that a young Teddy boy ought to be turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in drape jackets and drainpipe trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes averted are ones directed elsewhere, deflected aside.

clue.text: Trick by erstwhile yesman?

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
erstwhile means former or previous

explanation.surface: A deception carried out by a one-time sycophant.
explanation.definitionFit: A yesman goes along with everyone, someone who complies with whatever is expected.

clue.text: Communication taking a log time after muddle

indicators.note: after places the time word behind the muddle word

parts.note: a mess is a muddle
the clue as given reads log, evidently for long; an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A message takes ages to arrive after some confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'log' is a transcription slip for 'long': an age is a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A message is a piece of communication sent from one person to another.

clue.text: Brief description that is needed to identify coins

parts.note: spec is short for specification, a description
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A short description is required to identify old coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is money in the form of coin rather than notes.

clue.text: Rose, maybe — female less exalted

parts.note: lower means of humbler rank

explanation.surface: Rose, perhaps a woman of lowly status.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose looks like a woman's name; it is the bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose is one example of a garden bloom, flagged by maybe.

clue.text: Money for penning article showing remorse

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the article sits inside the money word

parts.note: pence are British coins, money
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer is paid for penning a piece expressing regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is a self-imposed act demonstrating contrition for wrongdoing.

clue.text: The bottom drain is broken

indicators.note: broken signals the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: The lowest pipe in the house has cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything.

clue.text: Whiskey producer's equipment is quiet

definitions.meaning: a distiller's apparatus for making spirits

explanation.surface: The distillery's apparatus is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A still distils spirits, and still also means calm and silent.

clue.text: Native American daughter making statement of faith

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: An indigenous girl declares her beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a formal summary of religious belief.

clue.text: Tolerate a bird

definitions.meaning: to accept or put up with

explanation.surface: Put up with a feathered creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow an insult is to accept it, and the swallow is a migratory bird.

clue.text: To obtain by coercion is no longer illegal act

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
a tort is a civil wrong

explanation.surface: Using force to get something is no longer a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To extort is to wring money out of someone by threats.

clue.text: Fancy screen that swings round in some churches

definitions.text: that swings round in some churches

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, signalling the letters reworked

explanation.surface: An ornate rood screen moves about in certain churches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swings round' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition; 'Fancy' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A censer is a thurible, a vessel of burning incense swung on chains during worship.
